Folks — quick engineering readout: we observe two correlated issues during autoscale events for the Hosted GPU pool: (A) kernel selection path introduced a synchronous KV-cache warm step that blocks first N allocations (regressed after kselect v3.1.2 deployed on Nov 3); (B) instance init (CUDA context and model shards) is taking 3-4x longer under certain image variants. Together they push cold-start p95 to ~6-7s and p99 ~12s for Requests that hit newly-provisioned workers.

Mitigation plan (ordered):
- Immediate (10–20m): Enable per-customer warm-fallback routing for PaymentsInc to a small set of kept-warm instances (will increase cost marginally) — this will route new sessions to already-initialized workers until the scale event completes.
- Short-term (24–48h): Disable the synchronous KV warm in kselect and switch to async background warming so allocations do not block request paths.
- Medium (3–7d): Rebuild image variants to reduce instance init time and add a graceful retry policy at API-gateway layer with client-visible Retry-After when appropriate.

I can flip the routing now if we have approval from Sales/Account (Priyom). Also attaching a dashboard screenshot (slo-dashboard.png) and a JIRA INF ticket I opened: JIRA-INF-4782.

— Dev
Principal SW Engineer, Serving Runtime

Subject: Executive summary: Incident INC-20261109-17 — Hosted API autoscale cold-start regression

Michael — attaching a short exec summary below that you can paste into your slide. Happy to jump on a 15-minute call with your CTO to walk through details; I can bring Dev and Marissa.

Executive summary (short):
- Impact: PaymentsInc experienced elevated p95/p99 latency and increased 5xx error rate during multiple autoscaling events between 08:48–10:05 PT on 2026-11-09. Symptoms included timeouts (504) and truncated responses for checkout flows across merchant IDs 4382 and 4391.
- Root cause: A recent change in the kernel-selection path introduced a synchronous KV-cache warm step that blocked allocations during scale-up. Combined with slower instance init times for a specific image variant, this produced a cold-start regression when GPU workers were provisioned.
- Immediate mitigation: Enabled per-tenant warm-fallback routing for PaymentsInc (routes ~8% to kept-warm instances) and temporarily increased warm instance pool size. This reduced p95 from ~6–7s to ~600–900ms for affected requests. Billing will credit incremental warm cost for the incident window.
- Timeline for durable fixes: 1) Disable sync KV warm and move to async background warming (24h), 2) Rebuild image variants to reduce init time (3–7 days), 3) Add API-gateway graceful retry + Retry-After behavior and automated warm-key management (2–3 weeks).
- Next steps: Deliver incident report (24h), postmortem and regression test coverage (48–72h), and a joint review with PaymentsInc SREs to validate warm-fallback behavior.

We're treating this as high priority. Please let me know a good time for the CTO call and I'll set it up.

Best,
Priyom
